A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ASTRAEA. Their main text, equations, algorithms, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite the expanded evaluation and reorganized presentation.

before.justification: V1 reports original Wan and OpenSora generation-quality, latency, memory, scalability, ablation, and sensitivity results, including detailed appendix tables.

after.justification: V4 retains original empirical results and adds HunyuanVideo evaluations, Sparse VideoGen comparisons, and additional qualitative examples.

M1.justification: The token score, query-only sparse attention, cached block outputs, and evolutionary budget search are retained. V4's pseudocode explicitly includes penalties, cached outputs, and parent retention already described in v1 Sections 3.2–3.3; these revisions clarify the existing procedure rather than establish a new proposed component.

E1.justification: The VBench text-to-video task and existing 2-second and 4-second 480P conditions remain. V4 adds a longer, higher-resolution generation condition: 5-second videos at 544×960 using HunyuanVideo. This modestly extends scenario coverage without introducing a new dataset or domain.

E2.justification: Sparse VideoGen, previously cited but not evaluated, becomes an actual comparator. SVG70% appears in the retained Wan 2-second and 4-second comparisons and the new HunyuanVideo comparison. Delta-DiT, PAB, and ToCa remain; the OpenSora comparator set is unchanged.

E3.justification: V4 adds HunyuanVideo evaluation configurations and specifies SVG's 70% attention-skipping setting. The Wan qualitative comparison changes ToCa from 85% to 80% reuse. Figure 5 also changes the stated OpenSora condition from 2 seconds to 4 seconds, without establishing a rerun. Existing evaluation metrics and the 30-generation search budget remain.

E4.justification: Table 2 adds a SELECTQ&K-labeled comparison addressing query-only versus joint query/key selection, while Figures 10–12 expand and replace qualitative cases. However, the SELECTQ&K row exactly matches the existing Wan ToCa2,80% results, so independent new measurements are not established. The earlier granularity ablations, sensitivity study, and convergence curves remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report five videos per benchmark prompt using different random seeds and report aggregate scores. Neither adds confidence intervals, variability estimates, significance tests, or a changed repeated-run reporting practice.

E6.justification: V4 adds substantial HunyuanVideo and SVG results, including detailed appendix metrics and new qualitative examples. HunyuanVideo ASTRAEA 50% reports 80.20 VBench and 1.93× A100 speedup. Table 1 also corrects Wan 2-second speedups: ASTRAEA 40% on A6000 changes from 3.88 to 2.35, and ASTRAEA 70% on A100 from 1.68 to 1.53, with unchanged latencies. Retained appendix VBench scores and FLOP breakdowns match.

T1.justification: The introduction corrects the token-length memory-scaling statement from sublinear to linear, a limited correction to complexity reasoning. The diffusion, attention, token-scoring, search, and FLOP mathematics otherwise remain equivalent; added temporal indices clarify previously documented use of earlier-step LSE values. No new proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The three principal contributions and headline 2.4× single-GPU and 13.2× multi-GPU speedups remain. V4 narrows the memory-scaling claim to linear, removes memory reduction from the conclusion's benefit statement, and foregrounds the previously reported greater-than-10-dB PSNR advantage in the abstract and introduction.

C2.justification: V4 adds a temporal-stability rationale for using earlier-step LSE scores and changes the recommended token-budget range from 30–40% to 30–50%. Appendix A.5 discusses earlier convergence and reducing offline search cost, replacing the conclusion's search-free future direction. The revised ablation interpretation incorrectly attributes greater-than-2% VBench drops to SELECTQ&K and TIMSTEP-LEVEL; Table 2 does not support those drops.

D1.justification: V4 clarifies input versus cached output tensors, expands algorithm walkthroughs, and explicitly discloses 30 offspring per search generation. It also supplies HunyuanVideo output dimensions and the A6000 execution limitation. Existing hardware specifications, metric implementations, search-cost figures, and project-access information are retained.

R1.justification: V4 adds Zou et al.'s dual feature caching work to the token-level related-work discussion. The main positioning against heuristic acceleration and expensive token selection remains. Sparse VideoGen was already cited in v1, so its new experimental participation is not a newly added reference.

P1.justification: V4 broadly edits the introductory, methodological, and evaluation prose, condenses the related-work descriptions, and substantially expands the algorithm explanations. The appendix is reorganized into separate algorithm sections and a detailed-results discussion. The title, author list, headings, and citation style also change.

P2.justification: V4 redraws the execution and evolutionary-search diagrams, expands Table 1 and the radar/scalability panels, and reorganizes appendix tables. The convergence figure moves to the appendix, while the original Wan montage is replaced by three larger qualitative figures covering three models. The document is also comprehensively reformatted.

improvement.justification: The HunyuanVideo evaluation and actual SVG comparisons strengthen evidence for ASTRAEA's applicability and speed-quality tradeoff. Clearer algorithm documentation and corrected speedup entries also improve the paper. These gains are limited by the duplicated SELECTQ&K result row, its unsupported loss interpretation, and retained blanket memory-superiority claims contradicted by the expanded Table 1.
